thesis: He describes progression from isolated chat to contextual workspaces, scheduled workflows and agent orchestration.
summary: Six user levels move from question answering through projects, connectors, human-approved operators, custom software and orchestrated agents. Martell distinguishes role context from workflow instructions, suggests packaging repeated work as skills, describes chaining and scheduling, and recommends planning before code. The final level uses a main coordinator, specialist agents and a critic; he promotes his Apex platform and a free playbook.

insights.title: Separate context from workflow instructions
insights.explanation: His ingredients/recipe analogy distinguishes who the user is from the procedure and desired output.
insights.quote: the master prompt is like your ingredients
insights.speaker: unresolved

insights.title: Package recurring useful work
insights.explanation: His three-times-a-week threshold is a personal heuristic for identifying a repeatable skill.
insights.quote: if I'm doing it more than three times a week
insights.speaker: unresolved

insights.title: Review a plan before software generation
insights.explanation: He argues planning reduces wasted iteration and token cost; no measured saving is supplied.
insights.quote: a whole completed plan that you approve first before it writes any code
insights.speaker: unresolved

insights.title: Give distinct agents distinct workflows
insights.explanation: The main agent delegates; specialist agents own work and a critic provides another model review loop.
insights.quote: each sub aent owns a workflow
insights.speaker: unresolved
